style: Say gently and expressively, like a grandmother reading a picture book aloud
lines: Black performers made the Cotton Club famous, but Black customers were kept out.
At the Savoy, people said you were judged by your dancing, not your skin.
At the Palladium, dancers from different New York communities shared the floor and exchanged ideas.
Bandstand used admission practices that kept Black teenagers off a dance floor showing Black music to the country.
Hank Ballard recorded The Twist before Chubby Checker made it famous. Both belong in its story.
Black and Puerto Rican young people in the Bronx made their own dance spaces and developed breaking.
Disco welcomed Black, Latino and gay dancers. Many saw the backlash as hostility toward those communities.
The Electric Slide raises a question: what belongs to a choreographer, and what belongs to everyone dancing?
Every dot on this line is a room where people danced. Tap one, and press Play to learn its steps.
Set where you stand on each line. Then pick two dances to put beside you.
